# Simulated demo output (not a measurement)

**Everything in this folder was generated by `python python/teg_analysis.py --demo`. None of it is real data.** The script builds synthetic CSV files from the ideal circuit model plus a little noise, then analyses them, to show what the outputs look like and to test the code before the hardware exists.

The plot legends say "measured" because the same plotting code is used for real data. Here, "measured" means "simulated".

Why the agreement looks perfect: the simulated data is made from the same model the script fits, so R² = 1.0000 and a 0.1% model-vs-data deviation are expected. Real data will be noticeably worse; a published study of the same TEC1-12706 module got 10-17% agreement (see [../docs/future-work.md](../docs/future-work.md#4-benchmark-for-the-model-vs-measurement-claim)).

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `demo_partA.csv` | Simulated open-circuit log while the bath cools |
| `demo_partB.csv` | Simulated load sweep, 100 Ω down to 1 Ω |
| `demo_partC.csv` | Simulated matched-load log at several ΔT |
| `fig1_seebeck.png` | V_oc vs ΔT, slope = Seebeck coefficient |
| `fig2_VI.png` | V vs I, intercept = E, slope = −R_int |
| `fig3_power.png` | P vs load R, with the zero-parameter prediction and a free fit |
| `fig4_dT2.png` | log P_max vs log ΔT, slope should be 2 |
| `results.txt` | All fitted numbers |

Re-running `python python/teg_analysis.py --demo --outdir demo_output_SIMULATED` reproduces these files exactly (fixed random seed).
